sections.title: Studies in Professional Practice: Designing Engagement
sections.description:
This course is an opportunity to participate in research, thinking, making and conversation project that will explore ways that community and design leaders can work together to catalyze transformational design, planning, and place-keeping from the ground up. The course goals are to learn from ambitious projects designed in community, to share knowledge and experience through dialogue, and to train ourselves for new practices of creative, collective action. The course involves two concurrent lines of inquiry. First, we will learn from case study projects that range from outstanding examples of community-engaged design practice to more radical roles and results of interdisciplinary work within movements. We will talk with thinkers and doers in community organizations, consensus organizing, public agencies, and the architecture, landscape, planning, heritage and art fields. We will consider how design can contribute to culture-shifting dialogue between public agencies, funders, and communities, and between communities and wider coalitions they might form. Second, students will design diverse tools and approaches to communication and engagement that advance defined goals. Students may work in a range of mediums according to their interests and the goals of the client, including video, print, social media, web microsites, data collection and visualization, events, happenings, digital libraries, tour design, geocaching, collective art projects, storytelling, installations. The aim is to design processes and engagement tools that help build community power and new forms of agency.
The course is planned for 12 students to allow for critique of work, site visits, and conversation in a seminar format. Course hours will include participation in evening community meetings on three Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday evenings over the course of the semester. Enrollment is open to all students. The more interdisciplinary the group, the richer the discussion and experience.
